ella: hey all, quick newbie q as i'm about to open my first PR to stats-worker: do we prefer rebasing onto main or merging main into feature branches? and i accidentally ran the build which added compiled artifacts — should those live in the PR?

hassan: welcome! :wave: for short-lived, single-author work we rebase onto main (keeps history tidy). long-lived branches or cross-team work — merge main. compiled artifacts should NOT be committed.

kyle: +1. practical flow for accidental compiled files: regenerate cleanly, then remove the generated files from the index and force-push. example: 
```bash
# regenerate to verify locally
make build
# remove generated files from git (keep locally)
git rm -r --cached path/to/build || true
# add to .gitignore if missing
echo "path/to/build/" >> .gitignore && git add .gitignore
# commit only the real source changes
git add path/to/src/*.go
git commit -m "feat(stats): add aggregation for X (ENG-110)"
git push --force
```
This avoids bloating the repo.

ella: thanks — also what's the expected commit message format? we use conventional commits?

hassan: yes conventional-ish. we prefer `type(scope): short summary (#TICKET)` on the first line, then an optional body with "Why:" and "Testing:". Example: 

feat(stats): new windowed-sum aggregator (ENG-110)

Why: supports rolling metrics for feature Y
Testing: unit + local integration with sample payloads

kyle: PR description should include Summary, Why, Testing, and a Reviewer checklist. If you touch infra/CODEOWNERS paths add the approvers. Small PRs get faster reviews.

docs-bot: docs-bot: FYI — PR template suggests adding "Reviewer checklist" and tagging related docs pages if any public API changes are included.

ella: got it. CI failed earlier on a generated proto diff. if i regenerate locally, how do i avoid committing proto/gen/*? CI still needs to run gen right?

hassan: exactly. commit only the proto source, not proto/gen. Regenerate locally to confirm no behavioral changes, then reset generated files from origin before committing: 
```bash
# after make gen
git checkout origin/main -- proto/gen/* || true
# stage only .proto files
git add path/to/protos/*.proto
git commit -m "feat(stats): add metric proto (ENG-110)"
```
CI will run the gen step and surface issues.

kyle: small extra: if you need to clean up many small fixup commits, do interactive rebase `git rebase -i origin/main` and mark fixups as squash/fixup. Keeps the PR tidy. We generally squash-on-merge.

ella: any guidance on PR size? my change is ~300 LOC and touches two small helpers + a proto.

hassan: guideline: if a reviewer can do a meaningful review in ~20 minutes it's fine. 300 LOC is usually okay if it stays focused and tests are included. Split if it touches multiple services or changes runtime behavior across boundaries.

docs-bot: docs-bot: quick reminder — if you change a public contract, update docs/ and include a link in the PR.

ci-bot: ci-bot: build #9987  queued

kyle: last nit: run pre-commit hooks (`pre-commit run --all-files` or `yarn format`) before pushing. Husky helps but running locally reduces CI churn.

ella: awesome — i'll clean the generated files, rebase, add the Reviewer checklist and ping here for a quick pair-review if CI is green. thanks! :pray:
